keyQuestions.text: How does the Product Owner parent route a request to a mode, where is routing logic stated more than once, where do the copies disagree, and what is the smallest set of routing sources that still serves the CLI, the hub and the Claude Project?
Which router copies are held equal by a gate such as benchmark/router/differential.py, and which drift unchecked?
Where is a hand-off between modes undefined, duplicated or contradictory?
Is routing embedded in the right Claude Project layer, and what could shrink without losing a rule that must fire every turn?
What are the concrete, ranked routing and mode-link changes, each with the files it touches, its risk, the gate that proves it and the byte effect on the kernel?
Which README claims are stale against the files they describe?
Which scripts, functions, flags and config entries are dead code?
Which references, assets, examples and playbook files are dead documents?
How does the Product Owner's own Python, shell, JavaScript and JSON deviate from the sk-code-skilled standards?
What is the ranked synthesis of every finding, and what can the repository not settle?

keyFindings.text: Hub SKILL.md rules 3 and 4 are both stated as absolute and contradict each other for a request that opens with a tool signal and also names an artifact: rule 3 sends it to the tool packet 'even when it names an artifact', rule 4 sends it to the default packet 'even when it names a tool'. Only the rule numbering resolves the collision, and no gold row covers that input class, because the nearest row inserts a leading 'run'. Fix: state first-match-wins in the rule text and add a collision row. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:54-55] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json:1-60]

ROUTER.md says no Product Owner gate runs the leaf-route replay, which is true of leaf-route-replay.cjs but reads as if the block were unverified. run_gates.sh does run the skilled hub contract, and that contract resolves every RESOURCE_MAP path on disk and against leaf-manifest.json. Fix: name the gate that does run, in ROUTER.md line 43. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:43] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/run_gates.sh:52-53]

Stage one routing exists in three forms that nothing compares as a set: seven prose rules in the hub SKILL.md, five ordered bullets in hub-router.json routerPolicy.stageOneOrder, and the Python replica route_stage_one() in benchmark/gates/check_hub.py. Only the gold rows compare them, so a rule no row exercises drifts silently. Fix: keep one prose copy in hub-router.json and reduce SKILL.md Stage One Rules to a pointer. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:50-58] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/hub-router.json:24-30] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_hub.py:239-268]

The compiled-router directive cannot fire for this hub: running it now returns the legacy sentinel, so five always-loaded lines in the hub SKILL.md describe a serving path that never serves product-owner. Either ship the activation manifest the directive needs or move the directive out of the always-loaded section. Fix: SKILL.md lines 40-46. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:40-46] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs:1-40]

The hub SKILL.md says check_hub.py checks that the hub files, the registry, 'the router' and the packets agree, but check_hub's router check asserts only two ROUTER.md frontmatter lines and never reads the intent model or RESOURCE_MAP; that block is held instead by the skilled root-router contract RRC-004 and RRC-006, invoked from a different gate row. Fix: SKILL.md line 82. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:82] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_hub.py:142-146] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/root-router-contract.cjs:13-25]

The same constant, DEFAULT_RESOURCE, names different resources for the same packet: ROUTER.md calls it the two Human Voice cards loaded on every request, while sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md sets it to references/interactive-mode.md. Both files present themselves as the routing authority a reader can apply. Fix: router-contract.md line 49. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:37] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:49]

The smallest set that still serves all three surfaces is four sources plus one implementation: mode-registry.json for mode identity, hub-router.json for stage-one policy, ROUTER.md RESOURCE_MAP for stage two, packet SKILL.md Section 2 for intra-packet detail, and router-contract.md as the one router implementation whose derived copies (route_contract.py, kernel Section 11) the differential gate holds equal. The hub SKILL.md stage-one prose, hub-router's stageOneOrder prose, routing.md's steps and check_hub's replica are duplicates of those four. Fix: hub SKILL.md and hub-router.json. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:48-74] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/hub-router.json:4-50] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:41-103] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:28-43]

The test that turns a FigJam mention into a paired second output is defined only in the prose and the executable contract (an output verb aimed at FigJam, or a with/plus/and join). hub-router.json's orderedBundle text and the hub SKILL.md outcomes name the exception without the test, so a stage-one-only reader cannot decide the pair. Fix: hub-router.json line 15. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/hub-router.json:15] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:79] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/routing.md:34] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:641-648]

The two maps each described as the single machine-readable projection disagree on key set: ROUTER.md maps nine intents including CLICK_UP and FIGMA, while router-contract.md maps ALWAYS, ON_DEMAND, TASK, BUG, DOC, STORY, FLOW and INTERACTIVE and carries no CLICK_UP or FIGMA lane at all. Different gates read each file, so no check compares the two maps. Fix: declare which file owns the lane set and derive the other. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:66-103] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:136-152]

benchmark/router/README.md says four guards fire independently, while the harness runs five: prose-table parity is guard 0 and main() calls it before the other four. A reader counting guards from the README undercounts the gate. Fix: benchmark/router/README.md line 151. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/README.md:151-166] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:691-705]

Coverage by surface, which is the direct answer to this question: intent routing inside sk-product-owner is fully gated across three implementations; hub stage one is gated only by 37 gold rows against a replica; the stage-two leaf map has its paths gated but its intent-to-leaf equality ungated; figjam type routing is ungated; kernel routing prose is ungated while kernel routing code is byte-gated. Fix: the three ungated rows need a gate each, and the two Leaf Maps need one comparison. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/run_gates.sh:41-54] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/run_fixtures.sh:36-39]

DEFAULT_RESOURCE in router-contract.md is read by nothing: route_contract.py has no occurrence of the constant, differential's table parity compares thresholds, regexes, lane maps, shape tables and the checklist but never this value, and its published value contradicts ROUTER.md. It is a dead constant carrying a wrong answer. Fix: router-contract.md line 49. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:49] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/route_contract.py:1-60] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:496-520]

Hub stage one is gated only by its gold rows: check_hub.py replays 37 cases against its own Python replica of the rules, and never parses the seven SKILL.md rules or the five hub-router bullets, so a prose-only edit that contradicts the replica stays green until a row happens to exercise it. Fix: benchmark/gates/check_hub.py and benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_hub.py:239-293] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:50-58] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/hub-router.json:24-30]

Only the kernel's code is gated, not its routing prose: copy parity compares Section 11 and checks that Section 11 is reachable from the kernel and from routing.md, but nothing compares Sections 2 and 7 to that code or to each other, so the always-loaded prose can instruct behaviour the router no longer has while every guard stays green. Fix: claude project/Custom Instructions.md sections 2 and 7. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:35-74] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:180-188] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:323-325]

The FLOW lane escapes table parity: differential compares RESOURCE_MAP lanes for TASK, BUG, DOC, STORY and INTERACTIVE only, and its coverage guard never routes a Flow intent, so the Flow pair and the figjam packet's type routes have no executable contract. The figjam packet is self-consistent, but nothing holds its type table, its route_flow() and the hub ROUTER.md together. Fix: add FLOW to the compared lanes or state why it is out. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:509-510] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/SKILL.md:35-57] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/SKILL.md:71-140]

The router-contract ALWAYS lane names sk-product-owner/SKILL.md, a path its own load guard can never load because the inventory is packet-relative; differential works around it by filtering the entry out before comparing lanes. The inconsistency is tolerated by the gate rather than fixed, so a second such entry would also pass. Fix: router-contract.md line 137-141. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:136-141] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:283-296] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:503-507]

The staging spec names sk-create-figjam/ROUTER.md as a router copy to compare, but no such file exists, and check_hub fails the build if one appears because ROUTER.md is in its packet-residue list. The figjam routing copy is its SKILL.md Section 2 plus its route_flow pseudocode. Recorded so the question is not answered against a phantom file. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_hub.py:52-54] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-create-figjam/SKILL.md:31-57]

The two leaf maps are validated by different gates that never compare them: ROUTER.md's RESOURCE_MAP is held by the skilled root-router contract for on-disk resolution and leaf-manifest registration, while router-contract.md's RESOURCE_MAP is held by differential's table parity against route_contract.py. Either map can change which leaf an intent loads without the other gate noticing, which is why the CLICK_UP and FIGMA lanes can exist in one map only. Fix: compare the two maps, or delete one. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:66-103] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:136-152] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/root-router-contract.cjs:13-25] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:503-510]

Three routing implementations are genuinely held equal. differential.py lifts the pseudocode out of router-contract.md, executes it as a module, and compares route_contract.py to it on five guards: prose-table subset, copy parity, table parity, behavior parity over 220 corpus inputs, and corpus coverage of every command, false prefix, topic and shape. It also requires the kernel to carry exactly one python fence and holds that block byte-equal, then AST-equal, to the pseudocode minus comments. Fix: none; this is the one sound routing gate. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:200-240] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:307-421] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:468-521] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:620-644]

Interactive Mode's clarification-lane sentence omits Task while the template it prints and the packet SKILL.md both include it: one line says a request that reached Interactive through the Doc, Story or Bug gate keeps that lane, and the code block beside it offers task as a prefix. A Task clarification therefore has a template and no stated lane rule. Fix: interactive-mode.md line 93. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/interactive-mode.md:87-93] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:125]

The Bug-to-Task hand-off is undefined at routing time. Bug Mode sends grouped bugs, consolidation tickets, bug-fix-plus-feature work and Refinement + Bugs tickets to Task Mode, but no router signal, framing pattern or topic reaches that decision: the contract routes bug and defect wording to BUG and has no grouped-bug vocabulary. Fix: bug-mode.md lines 43-47 or the topic table. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/bug-mode.md:43-47] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/routing.md:59-69]

The ClickUp hand-off has one owner but three pointer forms: the packet SKILL.md Section 7 owns it and says AGENTS.md and the kernel point there, doc-mode names 'Section 7 Push Targets', Story Mode names 'the skill's ClickUp handoff rule' with no section, and SKILL.md rule 14 names 'the transport contract in Section 7' although the transport contract itself belongs to the vendored mcp-click-up packet. The owner is right; the pointers are not uniform, and one is unfindable by name. Fix: story-mode.md line 412. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:173] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:281-293] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/doc-mode.md:416] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/story-mode.md:412]

The hub and the packet disagree about what happens to a Flow request the default packet keeps. The hub says that packet hands it on to sk-create-figjam; the packet's own Section 2 says two artifact commands are a conflict routed to one consolidated question. The gold row for $task $flow expects the default packet, so the packet's conflict rule governs and the hub sentence is wrong for the command case. Fix: hub SKILL.md line 60. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:60] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:59] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json:1-60]

The paired-output rule allows a Bug beside a FigJam board, but the bug scaffold has no Flows group to receive the board URL: the executable route forms the pair for TASK, BUG, DOC and STORY, while only the task, story, epic and doc scaffolds carry the destination. A bug with a diagram is therefore promised a link the artifact cannot hold. Fix: bug-report-template.md or the pair condition. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:670-681] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/bug-report-template.md:1-60] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/task-templates.md:55]

The Quick fallback is stated three ways. routing.md keeps the narrow Task fallback under Quick energy below the confidence floor; interactive-mode lets Quick bypass routine Task, Bug or Doc intake; the packet SKILL.md states the fallback with no Quick exception at all. A reader who follows Section 2 asks a question the prose elsewhere says Quick skips. Fix: sk-product-owner/SKILL.md line 62. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/routing.md:49] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/interactive-mode.md:109] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:62]

The Story bundle's task path exists in only two of the three places that define a task's output path: Story Mode and the task template say a bundled task saves as [###].[n] - task-[description].md inside the Story folder, while task-mode.md offers only the standalone task path and never mentions the bundle. A reader who loads only Task Mode writes the wrong path. Fix: task-mode.md line 22. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/task-mode.md:22] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/story-mode.md:388-401] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/task-templates.md:160]

The Story-to-Task boundary contradicts itself. Story Mode says a single implementation unit is Task Mode, and in the same section defines a Story as covering one or more requirements that become implementation tasks, so a one-requirement request is a Task by the first sentence and a Story by the second. Nothing states which reading wins before routing. Fix: story-mode.md lines 42-50. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/story-mode.md:40-55]

Two of the four documented energies have no route. The prose defines Raw, Quick, Standard and Deep, and lets a user ask for Deep or 'skip depth' for Raw, while the executable contract resolves only QUICK or STANDARD and carries no Deep or skip-depth pattern, so the same request routes Standard in code and Raw in prose. Fix: route_contract.py detect_energy and its fixtures, or delete the unreachable levels. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/route_contract.py:627-633] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:97-102] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/interactive-mode.md:73-77]

Routing sits in the right layer. The kernel is the only surface loaded every turn and Knowledge is retrieved by relevance, so a router kept in a Knowledge document routes a turn only when retrieval happens to pull it; that is why the kernel carries the decision code and why differential forbids any second routing copy in the knowledge root. Fix: none; keep routing in the kernel. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:84-97] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:384-394] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:35-37]

Section 10 QUALITY CHECKLIST BEFORE REPLY is a heading, a rule and nothing else: six lines and 133 bytes, with no checklist under it. In an always-loaded file it costs space for a gate that is not stated. Fix: claude project/Custom Instructions.md lines 317-322. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:317-322]

Section 11 carries 621 bytes of RESOURCE_MAP naming 17 references/ and assets/ paths that a Project cannot read, and Section 2 already says those stems map to Knowledge document names. The block is needed by the CLI router and by copy parity, so it is correct to keep, but its presence is a router-contract concern rather than a Project one and must be counted on the CLI side of any byte budget. Fix: router-contract.md. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:70-72] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:136-152]

Section 4's energy table presents Raw and Deep as selectable signals ('deep, think longer, full depth, complex multi-source work'), while Section 11's detect_energy returns only QUICK or STANDARD, so the Project promises two energies its own code cannot select and a Deep request degrades silently. Fix: claude project/Custom Instructions.md line 134 or the router. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:129-134] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/route_contract.py:627-633]

Section 5 duplicates guidance the same route already forces from Knowledge. Its three long paragraphs, Doc intake and source authority (925 bytes), the ClickUp layout contract (1,029 bytes) and the Story/Epic house format (3,168 bytes), total 5,122 bytes and each restates a document that Section 3 rule 3 requires on that artifact route. Keep the invariant sentences and the authority order, move the grammar and layout detail to the Knowledge docs that own them. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:150] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:158-160] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:85]

The kernel carries 18 Full detail pointer lines for only five distinct Knowledge targets, 1,657 bytes in all, one line per rule. Collapsing to one pointer per target saves roughly 1.3 KB with no rule change and no retrieval change, because every target is already named. Fix: claude project/Custom Instructions.md sections 3, 4 and 6. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:84-117]

The kernel states the knowledge-lane map three times: Section 2 Resource Domains lists the mode cards, Section 4's Primary knowledge column repeats them per intent, and Section 8's five-row consultation table states them again with triggers. No gate compares the three, so a lane added to one can vanish from the others. Fix: keep the Section 8 table and reduce the other two to a pointer. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:55-64] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:121-128] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:192-227]

The largest kernel block cannot shrink on its own: Section 11 is 588 lines and 27,025 bytes of the kernel's 70,010, and copy parity holds it byte-equal to router-contract.md minus comments, so any trim is a two-file change that also reruns the differential corpus. A proposal that quotes a kernel byte saving from editing Section 11 alone is therefore invalid. Fix: router-contract.md first, then the kernel. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:323-910] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:362-382]

What can shrink without losing a must-fire rule is 12,202 bytes, about 17 percent of the kernel: Section 5 at 7,597, Section 7 at 1,230 and Section 8 at 3,375, minus the authority order and the one-line house-format and ClickUp invariants that must stay. Sections 1-4, 9, 10 and 11 must remain because routing, ask-before-drafting, the Deliverable Block, the self-scan, the ClickUp approval and the router code each fire on every turn or on every reply. Fix: claude project/Custom Instructions.md sections 5, 7 and 8. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:138-227] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:228-322]

Change 1, highest value at low risk: make hub-router.json the single stage-one authority and reduce the hub SKILL.md Stage One Rules and Outcomes blocks to a pointer at routerPolicy.stageOneOrder and routerPolicy.outcomes. Files: SKILL.md, hub-router.json. Risk: medium, because prose is what a model reads and a pointer loses the worked examples in rules 3 and 4. Gate: the 37 gold rows in benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json through check_hub.py, plus a new assertion that the pointer names stageOneOrder. Kernel bytes: none. CLI bytes: about 2,632 from SKILL.md. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:48-82] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/hub-router.json:24-30] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/gates/check_hub.py:277-293]

Change 10: collapse the 18 Full detail lines to one pointer per target and drop the six-line Section 10 heading that states no checklist. Files: claude project/Custom Instructions.md. Risk: low, because every target stays named and nothing new is asserted. Gate: none automated; a pointer-resolution check would be three lines in the format gate. Kernel bytes: about -1,433. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:84-117] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:317-322]

Change 2, cheapest real defect: delete DEFAULT_RESOURCE from router-contract.md or give it the value ROUTER.md states, then add it to differential's table parity so it cannot disagree again. Files: sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md, benchmark/router/differential.py. Risk: low, because nothing reads the constant today. Gate: a new differential comparison beside CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLDS and the lane maps. Kernel bytes: none. CLI bytes: 51 removed or rewritten. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:49] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/ROUTER.md:37] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:496-520]

Change 3: state first-match-wins in the hub rule text and add the missing collision row to the gold set, a request that opens with a tool signal and names an artifact, for example 'figma-ds-cli fj nodes and write a task for the spacing', expected in the default packet. Files: SKILL.md, benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json. Risk: low, because the ordering already decides the answer and the task only documents it. Gate: check_hub.py replay, which fails today only if the prose and the expected row disagree. Kernel bytes: none. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:54-55] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json:1-60]

Change 4: correct the hub's Flow hand-back sentence so it matches the packet, which asks one consolidated question on two artifact commands and hands off only when the request is otherwise a single artifact. Files: SKILL.md line 60. Risk: low. Gate: the existing $task $flow gold row, which already expects the default packet. Kernel bytes: none; CLI bytes: a few dozen. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/SKILL.md:60] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/SKILL.md:57-59]

Change 5, the only change that alters an artifact grammar: either add a Flows group to the bug scaffold or remove BUG from the paired-output condition. The first keeps a bug-plus-diagram request writable; the second keeps the promise honest and is the smaller edit. Files: assets/bug-report-template.md or router-contract.md line 672, plus the corpus and format fixtures for either choice. Risk: medium, because it changes what a delivered bug may contain. Gate: differential fixtures for the route and benchmark/format/run_fixtures.sh for the scaffold. Kernel bytes: none directly, but the kernel's Section 5 house-format paragraph would follow a template change. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/router-contract.md:670-681] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/bug-report-template.md:1-40] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/format/run_fixtures.sh:1-40]

Change 6: resolve the energy mismatch in one direction. Either teach the resolver Deep and Raw and add corpus rows for 'think longer', 'full depth' and 'skip depth', or delete Raw and Deep from the prose and from the kernel's energy table. The first preserves a documented capability; the second is honest about a two-energy router. Files: route_contract.py, router-contract.md, kernel Section 4, fixtures and corpus. Risk: medium, because it changes a delivered route object. Gate: differential coverage, which requires a corpus input per energy before it can pass. Kernel bytes: up to about 400 if the table shrinks. [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/route_contract.py:627-633] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:129-134] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/benchmark/router/differential.py:620-644]

Change 7, highest risk and the one to schedule last: unify the leaf maps.
